# tiko

> tiko is a compiled, statically typed programming language for building fast, self-contained programs. Blocks say what they close (`end function`, `next`), and underneath is a systems language: generics, tuples, lambdas, typed errors (`Result`, `Optional`), channels and direct use of C headers, compiled through LLVM to native code for Windows, Linux and macOS, with no virtual machine and no garbage collector. Source files are `.tiko`, headers `.ti`.

An agent writing tiko code should read the AI Cheatsheet first. It covers the syntax, the standard library's entry points and the mistakes that most often break a build, and every program in it compiles and runs.

## Docs

- [AI Cheatsheet](https://tiko-lang.net/ai-cheatsheet.md): the language and standard library on one page, for AI coding agents
- [tiko by Example](https://tiko-lang.net/by-example/): one short, runnable program per feature, with the output it printed
- [The tiko Programming Language](https://tiko-lang.net/book/): the book, from the basics to complete projects
- [Feature Index](https://github.com/PaulSquires/tiko-lang/wiki/Feature-Index): one reference page per language feature and library module
- [Function Finder](https://github.com/PaulSquires/tiko-lang/wiki/Function-Finder): every function, grouped by what you want to do

## Optional

- [Compiler Error Messages](https://github.com/PaulSquires/tiko-lang/wiki/Compiler-Error-Messages): the `TKOnnnn` diagnostics
- [Compatibility](https://github.com/PaulSquires/tiko-lang/wiki/Compatibility): older code tiko accepts, and what it refuses
- [Source and releases](https://github.com/PaulSquires/tiko-lang): the compiler, the standard library and prebuilt toolchains
